title: How many of a public servants' savings and credit cooperative's first 2,400 payroll-deduction loans to members employed by private firms will go into default within the first year, forecast from ten years of payroll loans to public servants and the private employers' own payroll registers
subdomain: credit scoring and PD modelling (the first-year default of payroll-deduction loans to a new population of borrowers whose employers' staff leave far more often than the record's)
prompt_shape: one forecast count to the nearest 50 loans and each employer sector's share in default to the nearest 5 per cent; the savings deducted for 2026 and not received by year end by sector; the recoveries on 2023 and 2024 public defaults by unit type

distractors.why_relevant: the cooperative's own reported default share of its payroll-deduction book by year, which looks like the benchmark rate for a new payroll-deduction product
distractors.why_unused: it reports the public book's balance in default at each year end, a stock on a balance basis, not a first-year default count; no figure reads it
distractors.ruled_out_by: its own basis (balance 90+ days past due at 31 December, defaults kept for 24 months) and the product rules' default definition

distractors.why_relevant: unemployment and employment by branch of activity, which looks like a way to adjust a default rate for the private sectors' labour markets
distractors.why_unused: national rates by branch say nothing about the 38 employers' own staff; their payroll registers do; no figure reads it
distractors.ruled_out_by: the employers' payroll registers, which record their own staff month by month
